claim: HAP2 is a transmembrane gamete fusogen found in multiple eukaryotic kingdoms.
source: HAP2 is a transmembrane gamete fusogen found in multiple eukaryotic kingdoms and is structurally homologous to viral class II fusogens.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: HAP2 is structurally homologous to viral class II fusogens.
source: HAP2 is a transmembrane gamete fusogen found in multiple eukaryotic kingdoms and is structurally homologous to viral class II fusogens.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural comparisons and citations in the introduction.

claim: HAP2 is an attractive target for vaccines that block transmission of malaria.
source: Studies in Plasmodium have suggested that HAP2 is an attractive target for vaccines that block transmission of malaria.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations and experimental results throughout the manuscript.

claim: HAP2 has three extracellular domains, arranged in the order D2, D1, and D3.
source: HAP2 has three extracellular domains, arranged in the order D2, D1, and D3.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Monoclonal antibodies were generated against the D3 fragment of Plasmodium berghei HAP2.
source: Here, we report monoclonal antibodies against the D3 fragment of Plasmodium berghei HAP2 and crystal structures of D3 in complex with Fab fragments of two of these antibodies
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and described in detail in the Results section.

claim: Crystal structures of D3 in complex with Fab fragments of two antibodies were determined.
source: Here, we report monoclonal antibodies against the D3 fragment of Plasmodium berghei HAP2 and crystal structures of D3 in complex with Fab fragments of two of these antibodies
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 4 and Table 1.

claim: One antibody blocks fertilization of Plasmodium berghei in vitro.
source: one of which blocks fertilization of Plasmodium berghei in vitro and transmission of malaria in mosquitoes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: One antibody blocks transmission of malaria in mosquitoes.
source: one of which blocks fertilization of Plasmodium berghei in vitro and transmission of malaria in mosquitoes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The two antibodies cross-react with HAP2 among multiple plasmodial species.
source: The two antibodies cross-react with HAP2 among multiple plasmodial species.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 2C, D, and E.

claim: HAP2 is a gamete fusogen required for fertilization in eukaryotic plant, metazoan, and protozoan kingdoms.
source: HAP2, a gamete fusogen required for fertilization, is found in eukaryotic plant, metazoan, and protozoan kingdoms (Clark, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Crystal structures are known of HAP2 from Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, Arabidopsis thaliana, and Trypanosoma cruzi.
source: Crystal structures are known of HAP2 from the unicellular green alga, Chlamydomonas reinhardti; a model plant, Arabidopsis thaliana; and a protozoan parasite, Trypanosoma cruzi (Fédry et al., 2017; Feng et al., 2018; Fedry et al., 2018; Baquero et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: HAP2 can form a trimeric structure that is structurally homologous to the fusion state of viral class II fusion proteins.
source: HAP2 can form a trimeric structure that is structurally homologous to the fusion state of viral class II fusion proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: HAP2 fusogens have three extracellular domains, arranged in the order D2, D1, and D3, a disordered stem region, a single-pass transmembrane domain, and a cytoplasmic domain.
source: These fusogens have three extracellular domains, arranged in the order D2, D1, and D3, a disordered stem region, a single-pass transmembrane domain, and a cytoplasmic domain, and are expressed on the plasma membrane of male gametes or the envelope of viruses (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: HAP2 is expressed on the plasma membrane of male gametes.
source: These fusogens have three extracellular domains, arranged in the order D2, D1, and D3, a disordered stem region, a single-pass transmembrane domain, and a cytoplasmic domain, and are expressed on the plasma membrane of male gametes or the envelope of viruses (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: HAP2 is required for fertilization in Plasmodium parasites.
source: HAP2 is required for fertilization in Plasmodium parasites (Hirai et al., 2008; Liu et al., 2008)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Gamete fertilization takes place in the mosquito midgut in a blood meal taken from an infected individual.
source: Gamete fertilization takes place in the mosquito midgut in a blood meal taken from an infected individual.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about malaria transmission.

claim: Blocking fertilization prevents transmission to the individual from which the mosquito takes its second, final blood meal.
source: Blocking fertilization prevents transmission to the individual from which the mosquito takes its second, final blood meal.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a logical consequence of blocking fertilization.

claim: Plasmodium gametes emerge from infected erythrocytes well before digestion of the blood meal.
source: Plasmodium gametes emerge from infected erythrocytes well before digestion of the blood meal; specific antibodies present in the blood meal will react with and can agglutinate or otherwise neutralize gametes (Angrisano et al., 2017; Blagborough and Sinden, 2009; Qiu et al., 2020; Graves et al., 1985).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Specific antibodies present in the blood meal can agglutinate or otherwise neutralize gametes.
source: Plasmodium gametes emerge from infected erythrocytes well before digestion of the blood meal; specific antibodies present in the blood meal will react with and can agglutinate or otherwise neutralize gametes (Angrisano et al., 2017; Blagborough and Sinden, 2009; Qiu et al., 2020; Graves et al., 1985).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: HAP2 is present on male gametes (microgametes).
source: HAP2 is present on male gametes (microgametes) and has hydrophobic fusion loops at the tip of D2 that insert into the plasma membrane of the female macrogamete and trigger trimerization and structural rearrangements of HAP2 to the fusion state, which mediates membrane fusion and merging of the cytoplasm of the two gametes through a fusion pore (Kielian and Rey, 2006; Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: HAP2 has hydrophobic fusion loops at the tip of D2 that insert into the plasma membrane of the female macrogamete.
source: HAP2 is present on male gametes (microgametes) and has hydrophobic fusion loops at the tip of D2 that insert into the plasma membrane of the female macrogamete and trigger trimerization and structural rearrangements of HAP2 to the fusion state, which mediates membrane fusion and merging of the cytoplasm of the two gametes through a fusion pore (Kielian and Rey, 2006; Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Insertion of fusion loops triggers trimerization and structural rearrangements of HAP2 to the fusion state.
source: HAP2 is present on male gametes (microgametes) and has hydrophobic fusion loops at the tip of D2 that insert into the plasma membrane of the female macrogamete and trigger trimerization and structural rearrangements of HAP2 to the fusion state, which mediates membrane fusion and merging of the cytoplasm of the two gametes through a fusion pore (Kielian and Rey, 2006; Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: To mediate fusion, D3 of HAP2 folds over an inner trimeric core composed of D1 and D2.
source: To mediate fusion, D3 of HAP2 folds over an inner trimeric core composed of D1 and D2 (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Antibodies to D3 of HAP2 that block the interface formed with D1 and D2 in the fusion state might block fusion.
source: We reasoned that antibodies to D3 of HAP2 that blocked the interface formed with D1 and D2 in the fusion state might block fusion, as has been demonstrated with viral fusogens (Austin et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2016; Li et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a hypothesis based on analogy to viral fusogens.

claim: HAP2 D3 antibody taken up in a blood meal could inhibit fertilization and infection of the mosquito.
source: Thus, we hypothesized that HAP2 D3 antibody taken up in a blood meal could inhibit fertilization and infection of the mosquito and subsequent transmission to humans (Delves et al., 2018; Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a hypothesis and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Immunization of mice with HAP2 fragments or putative HAP2 fusion loop peptides has proved the concept that antibodies to different domains of HAP2 can block transmission of Plasmodium berghei or P. vivax.
source: Immunization of mice with HAP2 fragments or putative HAP2 fusion loop peptides has proved the concept that antibodies to different domains of HAP2 can, to different extents, block transmission of Plasmodium berghei or P. vivax, species that infect rodents and humans, respectively (Angrisano et al., 2017; Blagborough and Sinden, 2009; Qiu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The high-sequence divergence of HAP2 in Plasmodium species from structurally characterized HAP2 in other phyla emphasizes the importance of Plasmodium HAP2 structures for rational vaccine design.
source: However, we are far from having an optimized HAP2 immunogen. Furthermore, the high-sequence divergence of HAP2 in Plasmodium species from structurally characterized HAP2 in other phyla emphasizes the importance of Plasmodium HAP2 structures for rational vaccine design.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a rationale for the study.

claim: P. berghei HAP2 D3 (residues 477–621) contains four putative N-glycosylation sites.
source: To elicit antibodies, we expressed in Drosophila S2 cells a P. berghei HAP2 D3 construct (residues 477–621, containing four putative N-glycosylation sites) containing a C-terminal His tag.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Shaving N-glycans with endoglycosidase D decreased size and heterogeneity of D3 in SDS-PAGE.
source: Shaving the N-glycans with endoglycosidase D (Endo D) followed by gel filtration decreased size and heterogeneity in SDS-PAGE and confirmed N-glycosylation of D3 (Figure 2A, lane 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Endoglycosidase D treatment confirmed N-glycosylation of D3.
source: Shaving the N-glycans with endoglycosidase D (Endo D) followed by gel filtration decreased size and heterogeneity in SDS-PAGE and confirmed N-glycosylation of D3 (Figure 2A, lane 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Five IgG mAbs reacted with the immunogen with nanomolar EC50 values in ELISA.
source: Five IgG mAbs reacted with the immunogen with nanomolar EC50 values in ELISA (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Fabs of mAbs 2/6.14 and 2/1.12 bind with affinities of 5–10 nM.
source: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) showed that Fabs of two mAbs, 2/6.14 and 2/1.12, bind with affinities of 5–10 nM (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The epitopes of the 5 mAbs resided within residues 502–617 of D3.
source: Immunoprecipitation was comparable to the His-tag antibody, showing that the epitopes of the 5 mAbs resided within residues 502–617 and were unaffected by N-glycosylation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on immunoprecipitation data.

claim: The epitopes of the 5 mAbs were unaffected by N-glycosylation.
source: Immunoprecipitation was comparable to the His-tag antibody, showing that the epitopes of the 5 mAbs resided within residues 502–617 and were unaffected by N-glycosylation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on immunoprecipitation data.

claim: HAP2 D3 from Plasmodium species that can infect humans share 60–70% amino acid sequence identity with P. berghei.
source: As their D3 domains share 60–70% amino acid sequence identity with P. berghei, we tested cross-reactivity with the mAbs to P. berghei D3 using immunoprecipitation (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: mAbs 2/6.14 and 2/1.12 were especially efficient at recognizing D3 from multiple species.
source: mAbs 2/6.14 and 2/1.12 were especially efficient at recognizing D3 from multiple species (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: mAb 2/6.14 pulled down about 70%, 30%, and 20% of P. knowlesi, P. ovale, and P. malariae D3, respectively.
source: mAb 2/6.14 pulled down about 70%, 30%, and 20% of P. knowlesi, P. ovale, and P. malariae D3, respectively
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on quantification of immunoprecipitation.

claim: mAb 2/1.12 pulled down 60–100% of D3 from all species except P. falciparum D3.
source: mAb 2/1.12 was even more reactive, pulling down 60–100% of D3 from all species except P. falciparum D3 (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: mAb 2/1.40 showed strong reactivity to P. ovale, but not to D3 of other species.
source: In contrast, mAb 2/1.40 showed strong reactivity to P. ovale, but not to D3 of other species
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on immunoprecipitation data.

claim: mAbs 2/3.3 and 2/4.36 were highly specific for P. berghei.
source: while mAbs 2/3.3 and 2/4.36 were highly specific for P. berghei (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: mAbs 2/6.14 and 2/1.12 bound all species of D3 tested with ELISA EC50 values in the 1–1000 nM range.
source: mAbs 2/6.14 and 2/1.12 bound all species of D3 tested, as shown by ELISA EC50 values in the 1–1000 nM range (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Strong binding of P. knowlesi D3 to both 2/6.14 and 2/1.12 was observed with EC50 of <10 nM.
source: Strong binding of P. knowlesi D3 to both 2/6.14 and 2/1.12 was observed with EC50 of <10 nM.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: All 5 D3 mAbs specifically stained P. berghei microgametes.
source: All 5 D3 mAbs specifically stained P. berghei microgametes (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: mAb 2/6.14 at 500 µg/ml completely inhibited ookinete conversion.
source: Strikingly, mAb 2/6.14 at 500 µg/ml completely inhibited ookinete conversion and at 250 µg/ml inhibited by 96% (p < 0.001).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: mAb 2/6.14 at 250 µg/ml inhibited ookinete conversion by 96%.
source: Strikingly, mAb 2/6.14 at 500 µg/ml completely inhibited ookinete conversion and at 250 µg/ml inhibited by 96% (p < 0.001).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: None of the other mAbs inhibited ookinete conversion by >50%.
source: In contrast, none of the other mAbs inhibited by >50%, although mAb 2/1.40 showed significant inhibition at 500 µg/ml but not at 250 µg/ml (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Oocyst intensity was significantly reduced by mAb 2/6.14, particularly at 250 and 100 µg/ml.
source: Oocyst intensity was significantly reduced by mAb 2/6.14, particularly at 250 and 100 µg/ml (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Prevalence was significantly reduced by mAb 2/6.14 at both 250 and 100 µg/ml.
source: Prevalence was significantly reduced by mAb 2/6.14 at both 250 and 100 µg/ml (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: mAb 2/6.14 reduced oocyst intensity by 85% at 250 µg/ml.
source: Summing the results over all mosquitos in the three independent experiments showed significant inhibition of intensity at all three mAb 2/6.14 concentrations, significant inhibition of prevalence at 250 and 100 µg/ml of mAb 2/6.14, dose-dependent reduction of both measures over the three antibody concentrations, and a reduction of intensity by 85% at 250 µg/ml (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Diffraction data was collected and refined to resolutions of 2.8 and 2.1 Å with Rfree of 29% and 23% for complexes with Fab 2/6.14 and Fab 2/1.12, respectively.
source: Diffraction data was collected and refined to resolutions of 2.8 and 2.1 Å with Rfree of 29% and 23% for complexes with the transmission-blocking Fab 2/6.14 and cross-reactive Fab 2/1.12, respectively (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Table 1.

claim: Each structure has two independent D3-Fab complexes in the asymmetric unit.
source: Each structure has two independent D3-Fab complexes in the asymmetric unit, giving us four examples of D3.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The two Fab fragments bind to opposite faces of D3.
source: The two Fab fragments bind to opposite faces of D3 (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: D3 contains seven β-strands labeled A to E that are arranged into two β-sheets containing the ABE and DCFG β-strands.
source: D3 contains seven β-strands labeled A to E that are arranged into two β-sheets containing the ABE and DCFG β-strands (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: The way in which the sequence folds into this arrangement classifies D3 as a fibronectin type III (Fn3) domain.
source: The way in which the sequence folds into this arrangement classifies it as a fibronectin type III (Fn3) domain.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: The loops at the C-terminal end of D3 show markedly different conformations among the four examples of D3.
source: Comparisons among the four examples of D3 show markedly different conformations for the loops at the C-terminal end of D3, which abut the polypeptide segment that connects to the plasma membrane (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The loops at the N-terminal end of D3 show very similar conformations in all independent crystallographic examples.
source: In contrast, the loops at the N-terminal end that abut D1 show very similar conformations in all independent crystallographic examples.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: Three sidechains that support the hydrogen bond networks in the B-C and F-G loops, Asn-531, Asn-532, and Asp-598, are invariant in the 6 Plasmodia species.
source: Three sidechains that support the hydrogen bond networks in these loops, Asn-531 and Asn-532 in the B-C loop and Asp-598 in the F-G loop (overlined in Figure 4F), are invariant in the 6 Plasmodia species.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The two antibodies bind largely to opposite faces of D3, with 2/1.12 binding primarily to the ABE sheet and 2/6.14 binding primarily to the DCFG sheet.
source: The two antibodies bind largely to opposite faces of D3, with 2/1.12 binding primarily to the ABE sheet and 2/6.14 binding primarily to the DCFG sheet (Fab contacts are colored in green and red, respectively in Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In each Fab, both the heavy and light chain variable domains contribute significantly to the contact with D3.
source: In each Fab, both the heavy and light chain variable domains contribute significantly to the contact with D3.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: Fab 2/1.12 has the most contact with four residues in β-strands A, B, and E of D3.
source: Fab 2/1.12 has the most contact with four residues in β-strands A, B, and E of D3 (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: All four of the major epitope residues for Fab 2/1.12 are invariant among the species examined.
source: All four of these major epitope residues are invariant among the species examined here (Figure 4F), correlating with excellent cross-reactivity of mAb 2/1.12.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The major contacts for mAb 2/6.14 are formed by Arg-565 in strand D and six residues in the F-G loop.
source: Although mAb 2/6.14 contacts residues in each β-strand of the D3 DCFG β-sheet, the major contacts are formed by Arg-565 in strand D and six residues in the F-G loop (Figure 4F and H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4F and H.

claim: The F-G loop forms a large bulge on the D3 surface that fits into a cavity in the Fab centered between the three H chain CDR loops.
source: The F-G loop forms a large bulge on the D3 surface that fits into a cavity in the Fab centered between the three H chain CDR loops (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: D3 contains six cysteine residues, all of which are conserved among Plasmodium species.
source: D3 contains six cysteine residues, all of which are conserved among Plasmodium species; however, only four of these form disulfide bonds (Figures 4F and 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 4F and 5A.

claim: Only four of the six cysteine residues in D3 form disulfide bonds.
source: D3 contains six cysteine residues, all of which are conserved among Plasmodium species; however, only four of these form disulfide bonds (Figures 4F and 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 4F and 5A.

claim: Cys-513 in the A-B loop forms a short-range disulfide to Cys-523 in the B strand.
source: Cys-513 in the A-B loop forms a short-range disulfide to Cys-523 in the B strand that likely stabilizes the residues between Cys-513 and the beginning of the B strand, which are highly polar and mostly disordered.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: Cys-546 in the C strand and Cys-592 in the F strand form a long-range disulfide bond to bridge these two adjacent β-strands in the middle of the DCFG β-sheet.
source: Cys-546 in the C strand and Cys-592 in the F strand form a long-range disulfide bond to bridge these two adjacent β-strands in the middle of the DCFG β-sheet.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: Cys-542 is well buried in the hydrophobic core.
source: Cys-542 is well buried in the hydrophobic core.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: Cys-604 is exposed in D3-Fab complexes but in the full ectodomain may be buried by residues at the interface between D1 and D3.
source: Cys-604 is exposed in D3-Fab complexes but in the full ectodomain may be buried by residues at the interface between D1 and D3, including residues N-terminal to D3 residue 502, which were not present in the crystallization construct (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis and shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: P. berghei HAP2 D3 is only 9% and 18% identical in sequence to C. reinhardtii and A. thaliana HAP2 D3, respectively.
source: HAP2 D3 in P. berghei is only 9% and 18% identical in sequence to C. reinhardtii and A. thaliana HAP2 D3, respectively; however, their three-dimensional structures are highly conserved (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The three-dimensional structures of HAP2 D3 in P. berghei, C. reinhardtii, and A. thaliana are highly conserved.
source: HAP2 D3 in P. berghei is only 9% and 18% identical in sequence to C. reinhardtii and A. thaliana HAP2 D3, respectively; however, their three-dimensional structures are highly conserved (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The long-range disulfide bond that connects the C and F strands is conserved among P. berghei, C. reinhardtii, and A. thaliana.
source: The long-range disulfide bond that connects the C and F strands is also conserved (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Both C. reinhardtii and P. berghei but not A. thaliana have long insertions in their A-B loops and a disulfide bond that may help to stabilize these long loops.
source: Both C. reinhardtii and P. berghei but not A. thaliana have long insertions in their A-B loops and a disulfide bond that may help to stabilize these long loops, which orient quite differently (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: Asn-531 in P. berghei forms hydrogen bonds to both the BC and DE loops near the D1 junction.
source: Asn-531 in P. berghei (asterisked in Figure 5C), forms hydrogen bonds to both the BC and DE loops near the D1 junction (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: Asn-531 is in an N-glycosylation NX(S/T) sequon in P. berghei but its equivalents in C. reinhardtii and A. thaliana are not.
source: Invariance in the other two species, despite the evolutionary distance between the unicellular algae, the plant, and protozoan parasite, is of particular interest because Asn-531 is in an N-glycosylation NX(S/T) sequon in P. berghei but its equivalents in the other species are not (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The P. berghei HAP2 ectodomain is rod-like with three or four oval densities arranged linearly along the rod.
source: The P. berghei HAP2 ectodomain is rod-like with three or four oval densities arranged linearly along the rod (Figure 4I panel 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4I panel 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 2/6.14 Fab - ectodomain complex is L-shaped.
source: The 2/6.14 Fab - ectodomain complex is L-shaped (Figure 4I panel 2).

claim: Fab 2/6.14 binds essentially perpendicularly to one end of the HAP2 rod.
source: Fab 2/6.14 binds essentially perpendicularly to one end of the HAP2 rod, in agreement with the crystal structure showing that the Fab binds to the side of D3 (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A and 4I.

claim: The crystal structure of the 2/6.14 Fab-D3 complex cross-correlated well with the entire ectodomain Fab complex.
source: The crystal structure of the 2/6.14 Fab-D3 complex cross-correlated well with the entire ectodomain Fab complex (Figure 4I panel 3)

claim: The peak from gel filtration primarily contained a band at 75 kDa, in agreement with the expected size of the ectodomain.
source: The peak primarily contained a band at 75 kDa, in agreement with the expected size of the ectodomain; furthermore, its C-terminus was present as shown by detection of the C-terminal His-tag by western blotting (Figure 6B).

claim: Treatment with Endo D reduced the size of the ectodomain to ~71 kDa.
source: Treatment with Endo D reduced the size of the ectodomain to ~71 kDa (Figure 6B).

source: mAb 2/6.14 was fully reactive with the ectodomain as shown by immunoprecipitation comparable to that with the His-tag antibody.

claim: The other four mAbs were only partially reactive with the ectodomain, although they reacted with D3 comparably to mAb 2/6.14.
source: In contrast and surprisingly, the other four mAbs were only partially reactive with the ectodomain, although they reacted with D3 comparably to mAb 2/6.14.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on immunoprecipitation data.

source: Thus, the ectodomain appears to be only 0.88/9.1 = 9% ± 6% active in binding to Fab 2/1.12.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on SPR measurements.

claim: The ectodomain appears to be 130% ± 52% active in binding mAb 2/6.14, within error of the expected value of 100%.
source: Thus, the ectodomain appears to be 0.59/0.45 = 130% ± 52% active in binding mAb 2/6.14, within error of the expected value of 100%
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on SPR measurements.

claim: With Fab 2/6.14, much of the ectodomain was shifted to higher molecular weight and the Fab fragment was substantially depleted in gel filtration.
source: With Fab 2/6.14, much of the ectodomain was shifted to higher molecular weight and the Fab fragment was substantially depleted.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on gel filtration data.

claim: With Fab 2/1.12, only a small portion of the ectodomain was shifted to a higher molecular weight shoulder and there was little or no depletion of the Fab.
source: With Fab 2/1.12 in contrast, only a small portion of the ectodomain was shifted to a higher molecular weight shoulder and there was little or no depletion of the Fab.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on gel filtration data.

claim: HAP2 D3 bound well to both mAbs 2/6.14 and 2/1.12 in BLI measurements.
source: HAP2 D3 bound well to both mAbs 2/6.14 and 2/1.12.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on BLI measurements.

claim: HAP2 ectodomain bound to mAb 2/6.14 but not to mAb 2/1.12 in BLI measurements.
source: In contrast, HAP2 ectodomain bound to mAb 2/6.14 but not to mAb 2/1.12 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: mAb 2/6.14 binds well to both D3 and the ectodomain, whereas mAb 2/1.12 and three other antibodies bind well to the D3 immunogen but bind poorly to or do not recognize the ectodomain.
source: In conclusion, mAb 2/6.14 binds well to both D3 and the ectodomain, whereas mAb 2/1.12 and three other antibodies bind well to the D3 immunogen but bind poorly to or do not recognize the ectodomain.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from multiple experiments.

claim: This is the first time that a monoclonal antibody to HAP2 has been shown to block transmission.
source: Furthermore, we show that one of these antibodies potently blocks gamete fertilization and transmission and thus for the first time that a monoclonal antibody to HAP2 can block transmission.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a novel finding of the study.

claim: mAb 2/6.14 to D3 is at least fivefold more effective than affinity-purified polyclonal antibody to the fusion loop.
source: Surprisingly, mAb 2/6.14 to D3 is at least fivefold more effective than that affinity-purified polyclonal antibody, as 100 µg/ml reduced oocyst intensity by 78%, whereas 500 µg/ml affinity-purified polyclonal antibodies to the fusion loop reduced intensity by 61%.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on comparison with previous studies.

claim: This study is the first time that a defined domain from HAP2 has been used in immunization.
source: The present study is the first time that a defined domain from HAP2 has been used in immunization, that a monoclonal antibody has been found to be effective in blocking transmission, and that a Plasmodium species HAP2 structure has been reported.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a novel contribution of the study.

claim: This study is the first time that a Plasmodium species HAP2 structure has been reported.
source: The present study is the first time that a defined domain from HAP2 has been used in immunization, that a monoclonal antibody has been found to be effective in blocking transmission, and that a Plasmodium species HAP2 structure has been reported.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a novel contribution of the study.

claim: HAP2 is highly conserved, both within and between Plasmodium species.
source: HAP2 is highly conserved, both within and between Plasmodium species.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: In P. falciparum, 199 isolates evaluated have identical D3 amino acid sequences.
source: In P. falciparum, 199 isolates in PlasmoDB (https://www.plasmodb.org, release 54) evaluated have identical D3 amino acid sequences and only a few polymorphisms are present in D1 and D2 of HAP2 ectodomain in two or more isolates (R99E, n = 2; N184S, n = 14; D185Y/E, n = 11/7 and D455N, n = 47).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on database analysis.

claim: The high-sequence identity of gamete antigens contrasts to malaria vaccine antigens expressed by sporozoites and blood stage parasites, which have high levels of polymorphisms.
source: The high-sequence identity of gamete antigens contrasts to malaria vaccine antigens expressed by sporozoites such as TRAP and the C-terminal region of CSP used in the RTS,S vaccine and those expressed by blood stage parasites such as MSP1 and AMA1, which have high levels of polymorphisms and have proven to be challenging for vaccine antigen design (Neafsey et al., 2015; Takala et al., 2009; Barry and Arnott, 2014; Ouattara et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: P. berghei HAP2 is 60–70% identical in D3 to the five species examined that are capable of infecting humans.
source: Compared to CSP and TRAP, HAP2 is also highly conserved among species; for example, P. berghei HAP2 is 60–70% identical in D3 to the five species we examined that are capable of infecting humans.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on sequence analysis.

claim: The four residues most important for mAb 2/1.12 binding were identical among all six species examined, explaining the wide cross-reactivity of this mAb.
source: The four residues most important for mAb 2/1.12 binding were identical among all six species examined, explaining the wide cross-reactivity of this mAb.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural analysis.

claim: All three interactions by the Arg-565 sidechain would be abolished by the Asn substitution in P. vivax and P. falciparum.
source: All three interactions by the Arg-565 sidechain would be abolished by the Asn substitution in P. vivax and P. falciparum (Figure 4F), which had the lowest affinity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural analysis and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The rod-like, linear conformation of the HAP2 ectodomain and its monomeric state has not previously been seen for HAP2.
source: Thus far, structural information on HAP2 has been on its post-fusion, trimeric form or on isolated domains (Fédry et al., 2017; Feng et al., 2018; Fedry et al., 2018; Baquero et al., 2019). The rod-like, linear conformation of the HAP2 ectodomain and its monomeric state has not previously been seen for HAP2.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: The linear conformation of the HAP2 ectodomain resembles the linear conformation of pre-fusion states of structurally homologous class II viral fusogens, suggesting that this corresponds to its pre-fusion state.
source: Its resemblance to the linear conformation of pre-fusion states of structurally homologous class II viral fusogens suggests that this linear conformation of the HAP2 ectodomain corresponds to its pre-fusion state.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from structural comparison.

claim: The pre-fusion state is preferred over the post-fusion state as the target for transmission blocking antibodies.
source: The pre-fusion state is preferred over the post-fusion state as the target for transmission blocking antibodies, because antibodies that bind to the pre-fusion state not only can act earlier but can also sterically block the interfaces required for trimer formation and the fold-back of D3 onto D1 and D2 (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a rationale for vaccine design.

claim: mAb 2/6.14 might block conformational changes required for conversion of the monomeric pre-fusion state of HAP2 to the trimeric post-fusion state.
source: In addition to immunological mechanisms for blocking gamete fertilization in the mosquito blood meal (Graves et al., 1985), mAb 2/6.14 might also block conformational changes required for conversion of the monomeric pre-fusion state of HAP2 to the trimeric post-fusion state (Figure 1), especially reorientation of D3 to fold over D1 and D2 in the trimer, which is required for fusion (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis.

claim: Direct blocking of fusion has been demonstrated with antibodies to D3 of viral type II fusion proteins that are structurally homologous to HAP2.
source: Direct blocking of fusion has been demonstrated with antibodies to D3 of viral type II fusion proteins that are structurally homologous to HAP2 (Austin et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2016; Li et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Superposition showed that the F-G loop recognized by mAb 2/6.14 is buried in D3 interfaces in the postfusion state trimer.
source: Superposition showed that the F-G loop recognized by mAb 2/6.14 is buried in D3 interfaces in the postfusion state trimer.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural superposition.

claim: The mAb 2/1.12 epitope substantially overlaps with the D3 postfusion state trimer interfaces in the C strand.
source: The mAb 2/1.12 epitope also substantially overlaps with the D3 postfusion state trimer interfaces in the C strand.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural superposition.

claim: Both antibody epitopes overlap in the D strand with sites buried in the postfusion conformation.
source: Moreover, both antibody epitopes overlap in the D strand with sites buried in the postfusion conformation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural superposition.

claim: Binding of either of these mAbs to D3 would block folding back of D3 in the fusion state.
source: Thus, binding of either of these mAbs to D3 would block folding back of D3 in the fusion state (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from structural analysis.

claim: mAb 2/6.14 is differentiated from the other 4 mAbs studied by its ability to completely react with the monomeric HAP2 ectodomain.
source: mAb 2/6.14 is differentiated from the other 4 mAbs studied here by its ability to completely react with the monomeric HAP2 ectodomain.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on experimental results.

claim: Perhaps mAb 2/1.12 recognizes an epitope that is available in D3 but is masked or destabilized by association with D1 and D2 in the HAP2 ectodomain.
source: Among many possible explanations for this discrepancy, perhaps mAb 2/1.12 recognizes an epitope that is available in D3 but is masked or destabilized by association with D1 and D2 in the HAP2 ectodomain, and this inhibition by D1 and D2 is relieved by partial denaturation during fixation by paraformaldehyde.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation.

claim: D3 of HAP2 can elicit antibodies that block transmission of malaria.
source: In conclusion, we find that D3 of HAP2 can elicit antibodies that block transmission of malaria.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Some antibodies to D3 did not react well with the HAP2 ectodomain, identifying limitations of D3 as an immunogen.
source: On the other hand, we have also identified limitations of D3 as an immunogen because some antibodies to D3 did not react well with the HAP2 ectodomain.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Stabilizing the pre-fusion state of HAP2 may not only increase expression but also efficacy in inducing neutralizing antibodies.
source: Furthermore, stabilizing the pre-fusion state of HAP2, as successfully done for the respiratory syncytial virus fusion protein (McLellan et al., 2013) and SARS-CoV-2 spike protein (Hsieh et al., 2020), may not only increase expression but also efficacy in inducing neutralizing antibodies.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a suggestion for future work with citations.

claim: The HAP2 ectodomain contains 11 putative N-glycosylation sites.
source: The HAP2 ectodomain contains 11 putative N-glycosylation sites; however, Endo D treatment reduced the mass by only ~3 kD.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 6B.

claim: Endo D treatment of the HAP2 ectodomain reduced the mass by only ~3 kD.
source: The HAP2 ectodomain contains 11 putative N-glycosylation sites; however, Endo D treatment reduced the mass by only ~3 kD.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 6B.

claim: It is unknown how many sites are N-glycosylated in the HAP2 ectodomain and whether all sites are accessible to Endo D.
source: It is unknown how many sites are N-glycosylated and whether all sites are accessible to Endo D.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 6B.

claim: UniProt accession Q4YCF6.1 for P. berghei HAP2 ectodomain was retrospectively discovered to be deleted for S206.
source: UniProt accession Q4YCF6.1, which was used for P. berghei HAP2 ectodomain construct codon optimization, was retrospectively discovered to be deleted for S206, which locates to the βd-strand of D2.2 in the alignment to Chlamydomonas reinhardti HAP2, at the opposite end of the ectodomain from D3.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: All other eight HAP2 accessions recovered from the nonredundant protein database with NCBI BLAST in 2020 are identical to one another and differ from the Q4YCF6.1 sequence only at residue S206 and the signal sequence.
source: All other eight HAP2 accessions recovered from the nonredundant protein database with NCBI BLAST in 2020, including at least seven distinct P. berghei strains including ANKA, are identical to one another and differ from the Q4YCF6.1 sequence only at residue S206 and the signal sequence.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Among hundreds of sequences of human and mouse extracellular proteins of similar length, ~ 10% of UniProt but not RefSeq accessions have similar errors.
source: Our recent experience is that, among hundreds of sequences of human and mouse extracellular proteins of similar length, ~ 10% of UniProt but not RefSeq accessions have similar errors.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section based on the authors' experience.
